text:
Nina: Hey team, quick post-all‑hands consolidation on customer win/loss signals + asks. Wanted to get leadership alignment on which of these we should fast-track. Summary first: wins = predictable pricing + auto-fallback to quantized variants; losses = onboarding delays, opaque 5xxs during key rotations, and missing per-route audit for compliance.

Ravi: Can you share the concrete loss examples? Sales said one enterprise pulled out after a week of failing POC tests.

Nina: From notes: Customer A (regulated) declined after 3-week POC because they couldn't get a VPC proof; Customer B had intermittent 500s during load tests and no correlation_id to trace; Customer C found SDK samples confusing and stalled integration >2 weeks.

Elena: Add: two customers asked for a simple export of token billing per-route for security reviews. CSV would be fine. Also one asked for pricing scenarios showing retrieval + generation mixes.

Josh: Ops saw the 500s correlate with large batch evals on dedicated pools. ops-bot queued a report. ops-bot: run incident-correlate --range "2025-10-01,2025-11-30" --job 8121

ops-bot: Job 8121 queued by @Josh. Estimated time 2m. Results: https://internal/redwood/jobs/8121 (summary: spikes mostly from bursty evals + a handful of malformed key-rotation responses).

Ravi: For leadership decisions: Proposed priorities: 1) Make 5xxs diagnoseable (correlation_id + user-facing hint + KB link), 2) Shipping a one‑page integration checklist + SDK snippets, 3) Console CSV export for per-route token billing, 4) Pricing scenarios / small calculator, 5) POC concierge pilot for top 5 prospects.

ProductLead: Feedback: we commit to (1) and (2) as high priority. (3) is medium; we can prototype export in 3 weeks. (4) and (5) reasonable for Q2 but we'll produce templates now.

Elena: For (1) please ensure key-rotation paths include clear HTTP codes (403/401 vs 500) and that our LB proxies don't strip bodies. That was a root cause in one loss.

Josh: Agreed. Runtime will also add admission controls on Dedicated (throttle bursts >2x baseline) and a short-term mitigator: capacity guard rails for eval jobs. Adding to backlog.

Nina: Can ProductLead confirm owners and rough ETA for the high-priority items so sales has something to tell prospects?

ProductLead: Owners: (1) Eng Runtime (owner: Josh) ETA 4 weeks; (2) DevEx (owner: Ravi) ETA 2 weeks for checklist + code samples; (3) Console (owner: Elena) prototype ETA 3 weeks; (4) Product small calculator + 3 scenarios ETA 6 weeks; (5) CS + Solutions to draft concierge playbook in 4 weeks.

Ravi: I'll draft a short FAQ for sales that highlights wins (stable tail latency, auto-quantized fallback) and the commit plan for fixes. Will share draft here.

Elena: One request: can we anonymize and capture the exact quotes from the two customers that mentioned per-route auditing? Those are useful in compliance decks.

Nina: Drop them in the shared doc and mark PII redacted. Also capture the two 500 stack traces from ops link.

ProductLead: Leadership note: prioritize fixes that unblock deals quickly. Correlation ids + better error UX is highest ROI. We will treat the POC concierge as sales motion + CS; platform changes for admission control go to Q1 engineering roadmap.

Nina: Great. I'll collate into an action tracker and post link here. Thanks all. :raised_hands:
